surfaces.name: PingOne token exchange: trusted issuers
surfaces.oneLine: PingOne accepts a signed JWT from another issuer as the subject or actor token of an RFC 8693 token exchange, then mints its own access token.
surfaces.whatTrustIsFor: Trading a token from another system for a PingOne access token for one of your APIs.

whereConfigured.step: Add the issuer: Integrations > Trusted Issuers, then the plus icon. Environment Admin, or a custom role with trustedIssuers:create:trustedIssuer.

Assign it: Applications > Applications > your OIDC application > Trusted Issuers tab > pencil > tick the issuers > Save. The application must be OIDC-based with the token exchange grant. Worker applications are not supported.

Map claims: Applications > Resources > the custom resource that is the audience of the new token > Attributes > Add. For act, name the attribute act and use the expression {"sub": #root.context.requestData.actorToken.sub}.
Send the exchange with subject_token_type or actor_token_type set to urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt for the third-party token.

fields.name: Name
fields.meaning: A unique name for the issuer.

fields.name: Issuer
fields.meaning: The URL that identifies the external issuer. It is compared with the token's iss.

fields.name: JSON Web Key Set Method
fields.meaning: Either the URL where PingOne fetches the key set, or the key set pasted in (the jwks field is a JSON string).

fields.name: Audiences
fields.meaning: Accepted aud values. If set, at least one value in the token's aud must match. Blank accepts any aud.

fields.name: Require Expiration Claim
fields.meaning: Reject a token that has no exp.

fields.name: Require Issued-at Claim
fields.meaning: Reject a token that has no iat.

fields.name: Require Not-before Claim
fields.meaning: Reject a token that has no nbf.

fields.name: Clock Skew Tolerance
fields.meaning: Allowed clock difference in seconds, 0 to 60, applied when checking exp and nbf.

fields.name: Max Future Validity
fields.meaning: The furthest ahead an exp may be, up to 30 days. 0 means any future date is valid.

fields.name: Assignment
fields.meaning: Which applications may present tokens from this issuer. An issuer does nothing until it is assigned.

checks.orderNote: The docs do not state the order. Our measurements tested one fault at a time, so when two things are wrong PingOne may name a different one first. This lab runs them in the order below and says so.

errorEnvelope.prefix: The request could not be completed. The request was malformed or invalid.:

items.label: The token type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt
items.message: Provided token type must be urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt

items.label: The token is a signed JWT, not an encrypted (nested) one
items.message: Only a signed JWT is accepted as a third-party token

items.label: The calling application is allowed to use a trusted issuer
items.message: The token issuer does not match any Trusted Issuer for the requesting application

items.label: iss equals the Issuer of a trusted issuer assigned to the application
items.message: The token issuer does not match any Trusted Issuer assigned to the application

items.label: The signature verifies against the issuer's key set
items.message: JWT signature verification failed

items.label: exp is present when required and has not passed (within the clock skew)
items.message: The provided JWT has expired

missing.message: Missing exp claim; the Trusted Issuer requires an expiration time

items.label: exp is no further ahead than Max Future Validity
items.message: The exp claim exceeds the maximum allowed future validity

items.label: iat is present when required
items.message: Missing iat claim; the Trusted Issuer requires an issued-at time

items.label: nbf is present when required and not in the future beyond the clock skew
items.message: The nbf claim is in the future beyond the allowed clock skew

missing.message: Missing nbf claim; the Trusted Issuer requires a not-before time

items.label: At least one aud value is in Audiences (blank accepts any)
items.message: None of the token's aud values match the Trusted Issuer's configured audiences

refusals.symptom: The token issuer does not match any Trusted Issuer ...
refusals.cause: The token's iss is not byte for byte the Issuer you entered (a trailing slash, a different case), or the issuer is not assigned to the calling application.
refusals.fix: Copy iss from the token, not from memory. Then check the application's Trusted Issuers tab.

refusals.cause: The key set does not hold the key that signed the token (a rotated key, a pasted JWKS that is out of date), or the token was changed.
refusals.fix: Refresh the JWKS or switch to the JWKS URL so rotations follow.

refusals.cause: A Require switch is on and the issuer does not issue that claim. Okta and Auth0 tokens have no nbf. PingFederate client-credentials tokens have no iat.
refusals.fix: Turn the switch off, or pick a token type that carries the claim.

refusals.symptom: None of the token's aud values match ...
refusals.cause: Audiences is set and the token's aud is not in it.
refusals.fix: Add the audience the issuer really puts in the token, or clear Audiences to accept any.

refusals.symptom: Provided token type must be urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt
refusals.cause: The exchange named the third-party token as an access_token.
refusals.fix: Set subject_token_type or actor_token_type to the jwt type.

refusals.symptom: clockSkew must be less than or equal to 60
refusals.cause: The trusted issuer was saved with a clock skew above 60 seconds.

useWhen: A person's or a workload's token from another system has to be traded for a PingOne token for one of your APIs.
You want PingOne to mint the downstream token, with its audience set to a custom resource and an act claim added.
The other issuer is PingFederate, another PingOne environment, PingAM or a third party, and you can give PingOne its key set.
The trust is for one call at a time: there is nothing to register per caller.
dontUseWhen: You need to pin a subject or require certain claims. This surface has no setting for either; it only checks the issuer, the audiences and the time claims.
The token is encrypted or opaque. Only a signed JWT is accepted.
The caller is a worker application. Worker applications cannot be assigned an issuer.
You only want an API to check a token someone already holds. That is PingOne Authorize external OAuth servers (B), which checks and does not mint.

limits.text: Signed JWTs only. A signed-then-encrypted (nested) JWT is not supported as an input.
For a token from a trusted issuer PingOne ignores the p1.userId claim, so subjectTokenUser and actorTokenUser are null. This holds even for a token from another PingOne environment.
Deleting a trusted issuer removes it from every assigned application and those applications stop accepting its tokens. The page describes no disable switch.
Generally available in all regions from 10 Nov 2026, subject to licence entitlement.
Our messages and settings behaviour were measured on 2026-10-27, while the feature was behind a flag. They have not been re-run since general availability.
Whether trusted issuers can be assigned to AI agent applications is unconfirmed: the earlier guide said coming soon and the release note says only OIDC-based, non-worker applications.

surfaces.name: PingOne Authorize: external OAuth servers
surfaces.oneLine: PingOne Authorize checks a signed access token from another authorization server before a request reaches your API, then hands the request to your policies.
surfaces.whatTrustIsFor: Protecting your own API with PingOne Authorize when callers hold tokens issued elsewhere.

whereConfigured.step: Add the server: Authorization > External OAuth Servers, then the plus icon.
Set the audience on the API service, not on the server: Authorization > API Services > your service > Audience.
Associate the server with the API service, and deploy the API service again every time the server's settings change.

fields.name: Name
fields.meaning: Unique within the environment, up to 256 characters.

fields.name: Issuers
fields.meaning: The token issuer identifier. Add more than one with + Add Issuer. The token's iss must match one exactly, and the match is case-sensitive.

fields.name: JSON Web Key Set Method
fields.meaning: The issuer's JWKS URL, or the JWKS pasted in. The pasted string is limited to 16 KB.

fields.name: Clock Skew Tolerance
fields.meaning: Absorbs small clock differences when checking nbf and exp. Set too high it lets expired or not-yet-valid tokens through.

fields.name: Audience (on the API service)
fields.meaning: The aud value the token must carry for this API. It is defined on the API service, not on the external OAuth server.

checks.orderNote: The docs list the checks (issuer, audience, nbf, exp, signature) and do not say they run in that order. This lab runs the form and algorithm checks first, because a token has to be readable before anything else, then the listed ones in the listed order.

errorEnvelope.error: WWW-Authenticate header with an error code and description

items.label: The token is a signed JWT (not unsigned, encrypted or opaque)
items.message: The token is not a signed JWT

items.label: The algorithm is ES256, ES384, ES512, RS256, RS384 or RS512
items.message: The signing algorithm is not supported

items.label: aud, exp, iat and iss are all present
items.message: A mandatory claim is missing

items.label: iss matches one of the Issuers, exactly and case-sensitively
items.message: issuer mismatch

items.label: aud matches the API service's Audience
items.message: invalid audience

items.label: nbf, when present, is before the validation time (within the clock skew)
items.message: token not yet active

items.label: exp is later than the validation time, iat and nbf
items.message: token expired

items.label: The signature is valid and made with a key the issuer publishes
items.message: invalid signature

refusals.symptom: 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header; the audit event HTTP Request Policy Evaluated shows an issuer mismatch
refusals.cause: The token's iss matches none of the Issuers (a typo, or a token from another source).
refusals.fix: Make Issuers match iss exactly, case-sensitively. Save, then deploy the API service again.

refusals.cause: The token's aud is not the API service's Audience.
refusals.fix: Make the API service's Audience match aud, case-sensitively. Save, then deploy again.

refusals.symptom: 401; evaluationResult says token expired (or not yet active)
refusals.cause: exp has passed or nbf is still in the future.
refusals.fix: Check both clocks, adjust Clock Skew Tolerance, have clients fetch a new token before exp.

refusals.symptom: 401; the audit log shows an invalid signature
refusals.cause: The token was not signed with a key in the key set, or it was changed. A JWKS longer than 16 KB is also refused.
refusals.fix: Check the JWKS URL or the pasted JWKS holds the current signing keys. Remove keys that do not sign access tokens.

useWhen: You protect your own API with PingOne Authorize and the callers hold access tokens from another authorization server.
You want policies on the token's claims. The external OAuth server only does basic access control: claims-based decisions need custom policies.
The issuer's JWKS is reachable on the public internet over HTTPS, or you can paste it.
dontUseWhen: You need a new token minted. That is PingOne token exchange (A).
The token is opaque, encrypted or signed with a symmetric algorithm such as HS256.
The issuer's key set sits on a private network with a private certificate authority, and the pasted key set would be over 16 KB.

limits.text: Up to 25 external OAuth servers per PingOne environment.
Signed JWT access tokens, broadly RFC 9068. Unsigned, encrypted and opaque or reference tokens are not supported.
Mandatory claims: aud, exp, iat, iss. nbf is checked if present.
Algorithms: ES256, ES384, ES512, RS256, RS384, RS512. Symmetric algorithms such as HS256 are not supported.
The JWKS endpoint must be public HTTPS, answer GET, need no authentication and use no custom trust certificate.
JWKS responses are cached per server for 60 minutes when there is no Cache-Control max-age. A token with a kid that is not in the cache triggers a fresh fetch.
Claims with the p1 prefix are left out of decision requests when the token comes from an external source.
The documented rejection is HTTP 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header holding an error code and description. The page does not list the codes.
We have not exercised this surface ourselves, and no lab of ours configures an external OAuth server.

surfaces.name: PingOne Privilege: Federated Identity
surfaces.oneLine: The Privilege gateway trusts one issuer for one agent or service, so the caller holds no stored secret: its own platform's short-lived token is the credential.
surfaces.whatTrustIsFor: Letting an agent, a service or a sensor call the gateway with a token its own platform issues.

whereConfigured.step: The object is a Federated Identity in the console. Its API name has not changed: kind NonHumanIdentity at /api/{tenant}/v1/nonhumanidentities.
Ping's deck renames Non-Human Identity to Federated Identity as a display term (release 2026-11-02). Say Federated Identity to people and keep NonHumanIdentity in code.
A Federated Identity authenticates nobody on its own: an agent key whose custodian is the identity has to sit behind it.

fields.name: Issuer
fields.meaning: The expected iss, exact match.

fields.name: Audience
fields.meaning: The required aud. Mandatory: a token with no audience binding could be replayed elsewhere.

fields.name: Subject / AllowAnySubject
fields.meaning: Pin one sub, or explicitly accept any. Avoid accepting any unless the issuer is already tightly scoped.

fields.name: JwksURI or JWKS
fields.meaning: The gateway fetches and refreshes keys from the URI (preferred), or you pin public keys.

fields.name: MaxTokenLifetimeSec
fields.meaning: Refuse a token whose exp minus iat is longer. 0 means the gateway default of 3600. It is needed because a self-signing workload picks its own exp.

fields.name: RequiredClaims
fields.meaning: Extra claims that must match exactly. Use it when sub is composite, as in GitHub Actions (repository, workflow, actor).

fields.name: Platform
fields.meaning: A UI hint only (kubernetes, docker, github_actions, spiffe, oidc). It is never used to verify a token.

fields.name: Enabled
fields.meaning: The only kill switch for the identity.

fields.name: NotAfter
fields.meaning: When the identity expires. Empty means it does not.

checks.orderNote: The order and the wording of the gateway's refusals are our reading, taken from federated-identity-LAB's engine. We saw no accepted or rejected line in the gateway log for a workload token (see the open question below), so none of this is a measurement.

errorEnvelope.error: gateway refusal; the wording is not known

items.label: The token is a JWT (not encrypted, opaque or malformed)
items.message: workload token rejected: not a readable JWT

items.label: The Federated Identity exists, is enabled and has not passed NotAfter
items.message: workload token rejected: identity disabled or expired

items.label: The algorithm is asymmetric: never none, never HS256
items.message: workload token rejected: algorithm not allowed

items.label: iss equals Federation.Issuer exactly
items.message: workload token rejected: issuer mismatch

items.label: The signing key's kid is in the key set (an unknown kid triggers one refresh)
items.message: workload token rejected: no key for kid

items.label: The signature verifies
items.message: workload token rejected: bad signature

items.label: exp is present and has not passed
items.message: workload token rejected: expired or no exp

items.label: nbf, when present, has been reached
items.message: workload token rejected: not yet valid

items.label: iat is present and not in the future
items.message: workload token rejected: no iat or iat in the future

items.label: exp minus iat is within MaxTokenLifetimeSec (0 means 3600)
items.message: workload token rejected: lifetime too long

items.label: aud is present and equals Federation.Audience
items.message: workload token rejected: audience mismatch

items.label: sub equals Federation.Subject, unless AllowAnySubject is on
items.message: workload token rejected: subject mismatch

items.label: Every RequiredClaims entry matches exactly
items.message: workload token rejected: required claim missing or different

refusals.symptom: 401 with no explanation on the MCP door; no accepted or rejected line in the gateway log
refusals.cause: Unknown. With every claim matching, a PingFederate token was refused on the MCP door and the LLM route, and the check that should log the decision never appeared. We cannot tell whether the deployed gateway evaluates workload tokens on these routes.
refusals.fix: Ask Ping. Do not promise a customer that a workload token works on a door until this is answered.

refusals.symptom: Gateway log: non-human identity <name> updated, rebuilding 0 key(s)
refusals.cause: The identity has no agent key behind it, so nothing can authenticate as it.
refusals.fix: Create an agent key whose CustodianRef is the identity.

refusals.symptom: Spec.WorkloadIdentity and a NonHumanIdentity Spec.CustodianRef are mutually exclusive
refusals.cause: The key carries its own workload identity and also names an identity as its custodian.
refusals.fix: Leave the key's own WorkloadIdentity empty; the identity supplies the federation.

refusals.symptom: Spec.CustodianRef and Spec.UserRef name different principals
refusals.cause: A key cloned from one with a human custodian still has UserRef set.

refusals.symptom: PingFederate: invalid_target ... did not match any access token manager
refusals.cause: PingFederate accepts a resource value only if it is listed on a token manager, and our default manager issued opaque reference tokens, which can never satisfy an identity that needs a JWT, an audience and a lifetime cap.
refusals.fix: Add a JWT token manager whose audience and resource URI are the door URL, with a short lifetime.

refusals.symptom: Docker sensor loops: open /etc/procyon/nodesensor-signing.pem: read-only file system; then Unauthenticated reports
refusals.cause: The key directory was mounted read-only, then the key file was lost so the console still pinned the old key id.
refusals.fix: Mount the directory writable on a named volume, then paste the new key set from -mint-jwks into the identity.

useWhen: An agent, a service or a sensor must call the Privilege gateway with no stored secret.
The platform already mints short-lived JWTs: Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, SPIFFE or PingFederate.
You want the caller tied to one issuer, one subject and one audience.
You need to take one workload out of service on its own: Enabled is the kill switch.
dontUseWhen: You need PingOne to mint a token for a downstream API. That is token exchange (A).
You need an API behind PingOne Authorize to accept the token. That is external OAuth servers (B).
You must prove gateway acceptance on the MCP or LLM routes today. Our test did not.

limits.text: A key cannot carry its own WorkloadIdentity and also name an identity as its custodian, and cannot name a person as well.
Our live tenant had five such identities on 2026-10-21: a Kubernetes sensor, two EKS sensors, a Docker sensor and a PingFederate test identity.
The deck says the token is accepted across the MCP and LLM gateways (slide 40). Our own test of the MCP path did not prove it.
RequiredClaims is a native exact-match gate on a presented token. It is not Cedar.
Pass Agent Token forwards a presented workload assertion to a remote agent. A key caller carries no assertion to forward, so a remote agent set to Pass Agent Token refuses key callers.

surfaces.name: PingFederate: ID-JAG trusted IdP
surfaces.oneLine: A resource server's authorization server redeems an ID-JAG (an identity assertion) issued by another IdP, but only for an IdP it has been told to trust.
surfaces.whatTrustIsFor: Giving a signed-in person access to an app in another domain without a second sign-in (cross-app access).

whereConfigured.step: An IdP connection per trusted issuer, with the issuer as its entity id and its JWKS URL. Our script pingfederate/sync-id-jag-trusted-idps.js creates them from approved registry entries.
An OAuth client for the redeeming agent, with the EXTENSION grant type for the JWT bearer grant, and client authentication.
List the resource the agent sends as resource in an access token manager's selection settings.

fields.name: IdP connection: entity id
fields.meaning: The issuer, byte for byte.

fields.name: IdP connection: JWKS URL
fields.meaning: Where the issuer's signing keys are. PingFederate caches them and does not refetch for an ID-JAG without a kid.

fields.name: Client grant type
fields.meaning: EXTENSION, for the JWT bearer grant, with client authentication.

fields.name: Token manager resource URIs
fields.meaning: The resources the manager issues for. A resource not listed gets invalid_target.

fields.name: ID-JAG header typ
fields.meaning: Must be oauth-id-jag+jwt.

fields.name: ID-JAG aud
fields.meaning: The redeeming authorization server's issuer, as a single value.

checks.orderNote: These are the checks our own resource authorization server runs, modelled on the ID-JAG draft. PingFederate's order and exact wording were not measured, apart from the three refusals in the interoperability run listed below.

errorEnvelope.error: invalid_grant (invalid_target for a resource, invalid_scope for scope)

items.label: The assertion is a JWT (not encrypted, opaque or malformed)
items.message: invalid_grant: the assertion is not a readable JWT

items.label: The algorithm is RS256 (never none, never HS256)
items.message: invalid_grant: the signature algorithm is not RS256

items.label: The header typ is oauth-id-jag+jwt
items.message: invalid_grant: the header typ is not oauth-id-jag+jwt

items.label: iss names an IdP the server has been told to trust
items.message: invalid_grant: ID-JAG issuer is not trusted

items.label: The signature verifies against that IdP's key set (a key found by kid or x5t)
items.message: invalid_grant: the signature does not verify

items.label: iss, sub, aud, client_id, jti, exp and iat are all present
items.message: invalid_grant: a required claim is missing

items.label: aud is this server's issuer, as a single value
items.message: invalid_grant: the audience is not this server

items.label: exp has not passed (a few seconds of tolerance)
items.message: invalid_grant: the assertion has expired

items.label: The resource is one the server issues for
items.message: invalid_target

refusals.symptom: invalid_grant: The JWT header is missing the 'kid' property (from a third-party server)
refusals.cause: PingFederate 13.1.3 signs an ID-JAG with a header that has typ, alg and x5t but no kid. A consumer that looks the key up by kid cannot verify it.
refusals.fix: Needs a PingFederate change or a signing proxy. The server's own settings did not add a kid.

refusals.symptom: invalid_grant: JWT signature is invalid (from a third-party server)
refusals.cause: The issuer, audience, client and subject checks passed and the signature then failed.
refusals.fix: Not solved in our run. Compare the key the third party fetched with the key PingFederate signed with.

refusals.cause: The resource the agent sent is not listed on an access token manager.
refusals.fix: List the resource in the token manager's selection settings.

useWhen: A signed-in person must reach an app in another domain without signing in again.
You run PingFederate as the IdP that issues the ID-JAG or as the server that redeems it.
You can register each issuer once, with its key set, in the redeeming server.
dontUseWhen: There is no person: a service with its own platform identity should use Federated Identity (C).
You need PingOne to mint the access token. That is token exchange (A).
The issuer's keys change often and you rely on PingFederate refetching them: PingFederate does not refetch for an ID-JAG without a kid.

limits.text: An IdP must not redeem its own ID-JAGs, so the issuer is always a different server.
PingFederate caches the issuer's JWKS and never refetches it for an ID-JAG without a kid. After the issuer changes keys, restart PingFederate.
The issuer's key set should hold a single key, for the x5t reason in our guide.
Our interoperability run on PingFederate 13.1.3: Authplane accepted the ID-JAG, a public demo resource refused it (no kid) and Okta's sandbox refused it (signature).
The checks in this lab are our own resource authorization server's, not PingFederate's. The jti single-use and client_id binding checks are not modelled here.
